Modify or Extend Existing RTL: When extending an existing LUT-based phase module for new interface requirements, preserve proven LUT behavior and add clock/reset-driven one-cycle input registration to satisfy sequential timing checks without breaking phase accuracy.
Integrate multiple modules into a top mo: When integrating a control-heavy top module, treat unknown/all-ones inputs as invalid early, classify latency from pre-operation state, and keep output invalid encodings deterministic so functional and cycle checks pass together.
Create new RTL from spec: For scrambler/descrambler wrappers around PRBS cores, lock data/valid latency alignment to the testbench’s capture pattern first, because off-by-one pipeline staging can break both descramble recovery and checker-mode error timing even when bypass logic passes.
Debug/fix buggy RTL: For 2-way cache debug tasks, implement explicit per-way tag/data/valid/dirty state with deterministic hit selection and expose victim-way state so replacement and observability checks both pass.
